title: Motherwort tincture for anxiety palpitations
subtitle: A short-course tincture of Leonurus cardiaca for heart palpitations linked to anxiety
excerpt: Motherwort tincture is a 1:5 extract of dried motherwort aerial parts in 40% spirit, taken in small doses for the functional palpitations and racing heart that accompany anxiety or emotional stress. Traditionally used in European herbal practice as a nervine-cardiac herb for palpitations that are not caused by structural heart disease. A 50 ml bottle holds about 10 doses and keeps two years.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), motherwort entry, Botanical.com. Nicholas Culpeper, Complete Herbal (1653), motherwort entry, public domain. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Leonurus cardiaca L., herba (2010, EMA/HMPC/261931/2009), open access.

recipe.yieldDescription: 50 ml herbal extract (approx. 10 doses at 5 ml)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: steep 4 to 6 weeks. Finished herbal extract keeps 2 years in a dark glass bottle.

glossaryTerms.definition: A traditional herbal classification for herbs that combine a calming effect on the nervous system with a toning action on the heart, used in herbal practice for functional palpitations and anxiety-related heart symptoms.

projectSchedule.title: Start maceration
projectSchedule.body: Weigh 10 g dried motherwort aerial parts into a clean jar. Pour over 50 ml of 40% spirit. Seal and label with the date.

projectSchedule.title: Check liquid level
projectSchedule.body: Check the herb is still submerged. Top up with a little more spirit if needed. Swirl and reseal.

projectSchedule.title: Strain and bottle
projectSchedule.body: Strain through muslin into a dark glass bottle, pressing the herb firmly. Label with herb, spirit percentage, and date.

content.text: Motherwort herbal extract is a bitter extract of dried motherwort aerial parts macerating in 40% spirit for 4 to 6 weeks, strained and bottled. A

herb in the western herbal tradition, long prepared for the functional palpitations and racing heart that come with acute anxiety, fright, or emotional stress, where the heart itself is sound but reacting to the nervous system. The taste is intensely bitter. A 50 ml bottle provides about 10 doses. keep it for acute use, not daily dosing.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

items.prepNote: dried aerial parts, leaves, stems, and flowering tops

content.text: Weigh 10 g of dried motherwort into a clean steeping jar. Pour 50 ml of 40% spirit over the herb. Seal tightly and label with the herb name and date.
Store in a cool dark place for 4 to 6 weeks, shaking every few days. Check at two weeks that the herb is covered. top up with a little more spirit if not.
Strain through doubled muslin into a dark glass bottle. Press the herb well. Label with the herb, percentage, and date. Store in a cool dark cupboard.

2 to 5 ml in a small glass of water at the moment of acute anxiety or palpitations. Use as needed during an anxious episode, not as a daily ongoing dose. If palpitations are frequent or disruptive, consult a herbalist or doctor rather than increasing the dose.
Sealed dark glass bottle in a cool dark cupboard. Keeps two years from the date of straining.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use for palpitations comes with chest pain, breathlessness, fainting, or in anyone with a known cardiac condition or arrhythmia. These require urgent medical assessment. Motherwort is appropriate only for the racing heart of acute situational anxiety in a person with a known-sound heart.
